Cricothyrotomy — Surgical, Percutaneous & Needle

Finding the Membrane

One drawing, four procedures: the membrane is the cricothyrotomy target, the 2nd–3rd ring interspace is the tracheostomy target, the same membrane is punctured cephalad for retrograde intubation, and this is the anatomy you mark pre-induction in a high-risk neck before a possible CICO.

Cricothyrotomy — Surgical, Percutaneous & Needle

Needle Cricothyrotomy — And Why Exhalation Is the Whole Problem

If the chest does not come back down between insufflations, stop. Stacking breaths into a chest that cannot empty is how this technique kills people — and it is the reason a needle cricothyrotomy is a bridge, never the answer to a completely obstructed airway.

why-needle-cricothyrotomy-depends-on-the-upper-airway.svg

Retrograde Intubation

Stepwise Technique

The needle angles cephalad — the most commonly inverted detail in this procedure, precisely because cricothyrotomy, percutaneous tracheostomy and transtracheal blocks all angle the other way.

Transcutaneous & Transvenous Pacing

Confirming Capture — And Why False Capture Fools People

Both tracings have a spike before every wide deflection, and on a moving monitor they look alike. The difference is the discordant T wave and, decisively, whether there is a pulse wave beneath it — which is why you confirm with a femoral pulse, an arterial line, or bedside echo rather than the monitor alone.

true-capture-versus-false-capture-during-pacing.svg

Transcutaneous & Transvenous Pacing

Transvenous Pacing — Floating the Wire

If the ST elevation appears and then disappears, you have lost wall contact — that is not progress. Depth is only a sanity check: roughly 30–35 cm from a right IJ.

intracardiac-v1-electrogram-as-the-pacing-wire-advances.svg

Intraosseous Access

Proximal Humerus — The One People Miss

Internal rotation and the 45° caudad angle are the two things that make this line work, and neither is visible once the drill is in your hand. A needle driven perpendicular to the skin travels medially through the head and into the glenohumeral joint — it will stand up convincingly, flush poorly, and infiltrate.

proximal-humerus-intraosseous-access-in-two-steps.svg

Intraosseous Access

Proximal Tibia — Adult and Pediatric

The tuberosity is the reference, not the target. Adult goes proximal to it; a child goes distal — opposite directions, for the one reason shown here. Getting them backwards in a child puts the needle through an open physis.

proximal-tibial-intraosseous-landmarks-anterior-view-of-the-.svg

Resuscitative Endovascular Balloon Occlusion of the Aorta (REBOA)

The Zones — and the One You Never Occlude

Zone 1 buys the most pressure at the highest cost: every abdominal organ, both kidneys and the cord sit downstream. Zone 3 spares all of them. If the proximal pressure does not rise on inflation, the balloon is under-inflated, malpositioned — or the bleeding is above it.
